simple.meaning: חָמֻשׁ (châmush) is a Hebrew action word meaning “staunch , i.e. able-bodied soldiers.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 4 times in Exodus, Joshua, Judges, beginning at Exodus 13:18. The surrounding contexts include family, land, wilderness, Egypt, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to חָמֻשׁ (H2571) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: חָמֻשׁ (châmush) / H2571 is traced through Exodus 13:18, Joshua 1:14, Joshua 4:12, Judges 7:11 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H2571. chamushim חֲמֻשִׁים adjective plural in battle array , always this form, Exod 13:18 (E), Josh 1:14 ; 4:12 (both D), Judg 7:11 + Num 32:17 (JE), see חושׁ . חמת (√ of following; meaning unknown; Mv and others, very improbably, from Arabic grow rancid, putrid ; see on formation, Lag BN 154 ).
definitions.rootNote: passive participle of the same as 2570 ;
